PROCEDURES and GOTCHAS: task before branch (quest task start ... with --actor glyph-cli --actor-kind delegated-agent --accountable-human jdnewhouse); branch off origin/dev; tests live in test/python-hops.test.ts (probe/analyze helpers; append a describe block per task); format with bunx biome format --write src test; export PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.22.2/bin:$PATH; bun test takes about 95 s; typecheck, lint (one pre-existing warning), format:check. PRs: body in a file with --body-file; run git push and git checkout -b each alone in their own Bash call (a composed push or a commit while on dev is refused by a hook); never use shell variables in a path that is WRITTEN (the ownership guard refuses; use literal paths); the shell cwd resets, use absolute paths; gh pr checks can read 'no checks reported' for a few seconds after a push, wait until they register. Landing: only on the leader's head-pinned clear, bare and alone: gh pr merge N -R opum-ai/glyph-cli --squash --delete-branch --match-head-commit <sha> (with -R, gh does NOT switch the local branch: git checkout dev, git fetch origin, git merge --ff-only origin/dev, git branch -D the local branch; or git fetch origin dev:dev while on another branch), then confirm local dev == origin/dev and report the squash SHA. Never amend or force-push; do not push to a PR after it is cleared without telling the leader the new head (the clear lapses). A conflicted PR is fixed by restoring the conflicting record to its merge-base content in a new commit. Review: the leader runs dispatch-floor --pr N, then an Opus reviewer with NO shell; you create a detached review worktree under .claude/worktrees/review-GCLI-<n>-r<k> at the exact head (git rev-parse HEAD from inside it) and run the inputs the reviewer names from your PRIMARY checkout (the worktrees have no node_modules), reporting bins and edges verbatim for origin/dev AND the head. Report before pushing whenever the leader says so; leader messages cross with yours, so re-read the PR head before acting on a clear.

WORKTREES under .claude/worktrees/ (DEC-208: no removal until LCLI-740 ships; never remove another session's): review-GCLI-112-r1, r2, r3; review-GCLI-121-r1; review-GCLI-144-r1 (old head 2c3d901c), r1b (7ace2acb), r2 (a3ee204c); review-GCLI-146-r1 (a25c6fe5), r2 (3d9caead); plus older review-* and agent-* worktrees from earlier sessions. Detached, read-only; the ownership guard refuses git status inside a review worktree, use git -C <path> rev-parse HEAD. Local clutter not mine: chore/GCLI-67-session-handoff, chore/GCLI-77-*, docs/GCLI-*, feat/GCLI-75-*, fix/GCLI-56-b, test/GCLI-72-gate-scorer, tmp-gcli63-full, worktree-agent-* branches.

LESSONS from this stretch: (1) every unreviewed behaviour change is measured by running BOTH heads; never state one unmeasured (several predictions in review messages were wrong in both directions: the PEP 696 default IS parsed, N2 is a removal not identical). (2) The differential must vary the thing the change touches, including BINDER positions and not only READ positions (GCLI-144 round 1 and GCLI-146 round 1 were both blocked by a binder that moved scope); keep a positive control (the previous head must show head-only edges). (3) Removal-only is an invariant of the output, proved by a subset check, not by the pins alone (the five pins have been unchanged since GCLI-120 and prove little for rare shapes). (4) Every guard condition needs a fixture that turns its mutant red, or the task names it as untested: an untested condition is not a dead one (GCLI-147). (5) A mutant that stays green may be equivalent; say which, and add the input that distinguishes it. (6) Fix the mechanism text when a measurement corrects it (the default is refused by the superset rule, not the lazy rule): a wrong explanation in a fixture title misleads the next reader. (7) Do not push to a reviewed head with unreviewed bytes; use a test-only follow-up PR (a72). (8) Say 'not measured' and 'cannot be driven red' plainly. (9) When a hook or the ownership guard refuses a composed command nothing ran: split it, do not rephrase around the guard.
